mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% within a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances where the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% within a month indicates weakening labor market conditions, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors react to the economic slowdown.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances where the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) over three months suggests strong consumer demand, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings benefit from increased sales.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of the periods with sustained RSAFS growth.

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% within a month signals a contraction in supply, which often leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as it indicates a slowdown in economic activity.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the instances where the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 2% and the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.5% in a month, it indicates inflationary pressure, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as real returns diminish.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 2% and CPIAUCSL increases > 0.5% in 1 month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances where the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 100,000 in a month, coupled with an increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.3%, signals a weakening labor market, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS decreases > 100,000 and UNRATE increases > 0.3% in 1 month
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances where the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) over three months suggests a strong demand in the housing market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as it indicates a broader economic expansion.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of the periods with sustained HOUST growth.

mechanism_narrative: When GDP (GDPC1) growth is negative for two consecutive quarters and industrial production (INDPRO) drops by more than 1% in the most recent month, it signals a significant supply-side contraction, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as economic activity slows.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 negative for 2 quarters and INDPRO drops > 1% in 1 month
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the instances where the trigger condition is met.
